tier_reason: First-party Google Benchmark code is public (Benchmarks/benchmark_luabridge3.cpp, benchmark_sol3.cpp, benchmark_luabridge.cpp; Release build, embedded Lua 5.4.8), but no compiler, flags beyond the CMake build type, or CPU model are stated, so not A; the numbers exist only in the README chart image Images/benchmarks.png.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README chart Images/benchmarks.png (ns per operation, lower is better, 34 cases): against Sol3, LuaBridge3 is faster on 20 of 30 shared cases (member function call 152.4 vs 356.9, derived method call 91.8 vs 260.5, c function 44.2 vs 116.2, static member function call 88.4 vs 212.1, shared ptr pass 61.7 vs 123.2, userdata property getter 86.4 vs 165.5, userdata variable write 79.7 vs 161.2), slower on 9 (table get 29.1 vs 17.9, table chained get 69.6 vs 28.0, table chained set 56.5 vs 26.8, table global string get 39.7 vs 11.9, table set 18.3 vs 17.2, multi return 49.7 vs 44.8, stateful function object 40.0 vs 37.4, c function through lua in c 40.4 vs 34.3, lua function in c 26.8 vs 25.7) and tied on optional failure (14.3). Against vanilla LuaBridge it is faster on 12 of 22 shared cases (table get 29.1 vs 57.1, optional success 26.8 vs 110.0, table chained get 69.6 vs 156.7) and slower on 10 (c function 44.2 vs 34.3, member function call 152.4 vs 148.7, static member function call 88.4 vs 60.9, lambda capture 45.1 vs 32.8, multi return lua 48.3 vs 33.0, return userdata 167.2 vs 142.0). The headline userdata variable access rows (70.2 vs Sol3 299.9 and vanilla 269.3) are not like-for-like: LuaBridge3's script does one read, the other two do two reads and a write. Win/loss counts derived from page data.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: CMake Release build (Benchmarks/README.md), Google Benchmark v1.8.4, Lua 5.4.8 sources compiled into each executable; Sol3 built with SOL_ALL_SAFETIES_ON=1 and SOL_NO_EXCEPTIONS=1. No LTO flag is set in the CMake files despite the README's link-time-optimization wording; compiler and compiler version not stated.
corrections.workload: Per-operation binding overhead in nanoseconds across 34 cases (global and table get/set, chained table access, free, member, static and derived method calls, userdata properties, shared-pointer ownership, multi-return, lambda captures, optionals, converters), Google Benchmark, all three libraries on embedded Lua 5.4.8, each case in isolation.
corrections.caveats: First-party chart only, embedded as an image (Images/benchmarks.png); no hardware, compiler or compiler version stated. Harness is not like-for-like: (1) userdata variable access, access large and access last run 'return b.var' for LuaBridge3 but 'b.var = b.var + 1.0 return b.var' (two reads plus a write) for Sol3 and vanilla LuaBridge, so the largest claimed wins (70.2 vs 299.9 ns) compare one operation against three; (2) LuaBridge3 and vanilla cases invoke the Lua script with raw lua_getglobal + lua_pcall while every Sol3 script case goes through sol's lua["name"]() proxy lookup and call each iteration, adding C++-side overhead only to Sol3 (Sol3 c function 116.2 vs c function through lua in c 34.3, a gap of about 82 ns that LuaBridge3 does not show, 44.2 vs 40.4; rough inference derived from page data). On cases that use each library's own C++ API on both sides (table get/set, chained, global get, multi return, stateful function object), Sol3 is mostly faster. Vanilla LuaBridge beats LuaBridge3 on 10 of 22 shared cases, mostly call paths. Sol2 version is ambiguous: Benchmarks/CMakeLists.txt pins v3.3.0 while Benchmarks/README.md says v3.5.0, and vanilla LuaBridge is fetched from master. README says it 'competes directly with sol2', not that it beats it. Baseline (other binding libraries) is not in the category list (Lua, Duktape, QuickJS). Derived from vinniefalco/LuaBridge per README.

notes: Numbers in the record match the chart, but the claim is overstated: the biggest wins (userdata variable access 70.2 vs 299.9/269.3 ns) time one property read for LuaBridge3 against a read-modify-write-read for Sol3 and vanilla, and every Sol3 script case pays an extra lua["name"]() proxy call that the LuaBridge3 harness avoids with raw lua_pcall. Keep at C with harness flaws documented; it is slower than vanilla LuaBridge on 10 of 22 shared cases and slower than Sol3 on most C++-side table cases.

tier_reason: First-party performance guide gives ratios only (table.sort ~4x, table insert/remove/move 3x and more vs un-tuned versions, paged sweeper 2-3x vs Lua/LuaJIT linked-list sweep, table length 50+%) with no workloads, hardware, compiler flags or raw numbers; the interpreter-vs-Lua 5.x claim has no number at all. bench/bench.py can compare VMs but no results are checked in. An independent Are-we-fast-yet run exists but compares against LuaJIT, not PUC Lua, so it does not lift the tier.

corrections.caveats: First-party documentation page with ratios but no workload list, hardware, compiler flags or raw numbers, so tier C. The interpreter claim ('noticeably faster than Lua 5.x ... Lua 5.4 ... doesn't come close') has no number; the ~4x table.sort figure names no baseline; table insert/remove/move 3x is 'compared to un-tuned versions'; the 50+% table length gain is versus the default binary search computed from scratch. The repo has bench/ (bench.py with --compare for other VMs, micro_tests, gc) but no checked-in result tables. Several gains (fastcall builtins, imports) require the sandboxed pure global environment and are deoptimized by loadstring/getfenv/setfenv. Independent data point against a different baseline: rochus-keller/Are-we-fast-yet Luau/Results.pdf (14 Are-we-fast-yet benchmarks, i5-8350U, GCC 12.2.0, Luau commit 5836a9c, make config=release, 2025-10-25) gives geomean factors relative to LuaJIT 2.1 JIT of 2.39 for Luau default, 2.31 for -g0 -O2, 1.64 for -O2 --codegen, versus 2.32 for LuaJIT -joff; that is, the Luau interpreter is roughly at LuaJIT interpreter speed (about 3% slower), with no PUC Lua 5.x column.

notes: Record matches the performance guide; tier C stands. Ratio claims are first-party and loosely baselined; the core interpreter-vs-Lua 5.4 claim has no number. The independent Are-we-fast-yet Results.pdf (i5-8350U, GCC 12.2.0) shows Luau's interpreter about level with LuaJIT 2.1 -joff (geomean 2.39 vs 2.32), useful for the enricher, but it has no PUC Lua column.

tier_reason: The benchmarks page is first-party (2018) with graphs only and no numbers in text; the lua-bindings-shootout code is public but states no compiler, flags or CPU, so C. A third-party suite (satoren/lua_binding_benchmark: i5-4460, GCC 5.3.1, CMake Release, code public) exists but tests sol2 v2.5.1 from 2016 and shows mixed results, so it does not support an upgrade.

corrections.caveats: Evidence is first-party graphs from 2018 (page dated May 17th, 2018) from the author's own lua-bindings-shootout (nonius, Lua 5.3.3 DLL per the docs page; shootout README lists plain C on Lua 5.3.4, sol2 v2.20.0 and sol3 'latest'); no numbers in text and no hardware, compiler or flags stated. Approximate values read off benchmark_results/member function call.png: plain_c about 115 ns, sol3 about 135, oolua about 145, sol2 about 150, luwra about 205, luabridge about 420, old sol about 425, toluapp about 590 (read from the image, not text). Third-party counter-evidence: satoren/lua_binding_benchmark result/result.csv (Intel Core i5-4460, GCC 5.3.1, CMake Release, units not stated, lower is better) puts sol2 v2.5.1 fastest among bindings on global table (338.4) and table chain (561.0, below plain API 596.5), but behind kaguya (1006.9), luacppinterface (1002.0) and the plain API (1086.6) on C++ object member call (sol2 1342.9), behind luwra on C function call (234.7 vs 254.8) and returning a class object (1253.3 vs 1314.4), and behind sol v1 on Lua function call (293.4 vs 330.0). A 2026 first-party chart in the LuaBridge3 README shows Sol3 slower than LuaBridge3 on most script-invoked cases (member function call 356.9 vs 152.4 ns) but faster on C++-side table get/set; that harness is biased against Sol3 (extra lua["name"]() call per iteration, unequal userdata access scripts). Binding-layer overhead, not script execution speed; every binding is slower than the plain Lua C API. Baseline (other binding libraries) is not in the category list (Lua, Duktape, QuickJS). Last commit 2025-03-07, so stale.

notes: Record is accurate: README says 'Fastest in the land' and the docs page says sol 'seems to take the cake in most categories', with graphs only. Keep at C; add that the only independent suite found (satoren, i5-4460, GCC 5.3.1, sol2 v2.5.1, 2016) shows sol2 winning 2 of 6 categories and mid-pack on member calls, and that all evidence predates current sol3 releases.
